With a weaving legacy in Kerala dating back over a century, Neytt is finding new ways to bring textile craft into contemporary homes. The design house, which has also created a carpet for the Met Gala, moves beyond floor coverings with its 1854 Collection, a series of woven artwork made from raw sisal, New Zealand wool and bamboo silk.
Inspired by postage stamps, the collection translates Indian landmarks and cultural landscapes into tactile compositions. Delhi’s Qutub Minar, Mumbai’s Gateway of India and Kochi’s backwaters become textile portraits, bringing architecture and memory to the walls.
